findings.claim: The README instructs users to install the pinned stable pair `@3.0.5`, but the DevTools feature documented immediately below in the same README is only in the `Unreleased` changelog section and is not present in 3.0.5.
findings.evidence: The install hunk replaces the `@next` guidance with `pnpm add @prometheus-ags/entity-graph-core@3.0.5 @prometheus-ags/prometheus-entity-management@3.0.5`, while the CHANGELOG hunk adds the inspector under a new `## Unreleased` heading above `## 3.0.5`, proving 3.0.5 predates the `./devtools` entries. A consumer following these instructions gets a package with no `./devtools` or `./devtools/auto` subpath, and the documented import (`@prometheus-ags/prometheus-entity-management/devtools/auto`) fails to resolve.
findings.suggested_fix: Either hold the DevTools documentation until the feature version is published and pin to that version, or keep explicit prerelease/RC install guidance for the inspector entries and label the section as unreleased.

findings.claim: The ledger format changes from a flat array of export names to an entry-point-keyed object, but no consumer of this file other than the registry is updated in the diff.
findings.evidence: The hunk rewrites the entire file from `["ActionButtonRow", ...]` to `{ ".": [...], "./devtools": [...], "./devtools/auto": [...] }`. The file tree shows other scripts that plausibly parse this ledger — `scripts/verify-skills-exports.mjs`, `scripts/verify-skills-snippets.mjs`, `scripts/verify-skills-ecosystem.mjs`, `scripts/refresh-exports-ledger.mjs` — none of which appear in the diff. Any consumer doing `ledger.includes(name)` or iterating it as an array silently breaks or fails open.
findings.suggested_fix: Show or add updates to every script that reads `library-exports.json` so they handle the keyed-object shape, and confirm `verify:skills` passes with the new format.

findings.claim: The hardcoded `REEXPORT_DOCS` fallback lets the documentation gate pass with invented, stale text even when the real source JSDoc is missing or changed, and the map is applied globally across all 12 packages rather than scoped to the React package.
findings.evidence: `const REEXPORT_DOCS = Object.freeze({ configureTimeTravel: "Deprecated compatibility facade...", EntityGraphDevtools: "SSR-safe explicit host...", ... })` is consulted as `REEXPORT_DOCS[name]` inside the per-package loop with no package qualifier. If a symbol's actual documentation is deleted or edited, the frozen string still satisfies the `documented` check, masking the regression the gate exists to catch; the same text is also injected for any same-named export in another package (e.g. `configureTimeTravel` in entity-graph-core).
findings.suggested_fix: Scope the fallback per package and entry, or fail the gate when TypeDoc drops a documented re-export instead of substituting hardcoded copy.

findings.claim: A hand-written `## Unreleased` section is added to a changesets-managed changelog, and the addition of two new public export subpaths is classified as a patch change.
findings.evidence: The file tree contains a `.changeset/` directory with `config.json`, meaning changelogs are generated by changesets at release time; manual `Unreleased` entries are not consumed by `changeset version` and will be orphaned or conflict. The entry itself — `Add an optional React entity-graph inspector at ./devtools plus ... ./devtools/auto` — adds new public API surface (`./devtools`, `./devtools/auto` in the exports ledger), which is a minor-level feature, not a patch.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the manual section with a changeset file under `.changeset/` declaring a minor bump for `@prometheus-ags/prometheus-entity-management`.

findings.claim: The packed browser acceptance evidence was recorded against a dirty working tree, so the recorded commit and package sha256 do not fully determine what was actually tested.
findings.evidence: `"source": { "commit": "8e1cefaa0e2f60a68e138178631ef0757a0c261d", "dirtyTaskFiles": true }` — the gate that task 11 requires to prove production exclusion and packed-consumer behavior ran with uncommitted task-file modifications, meaning the evidence cannot be reproduced from the recorded commit alone.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-run the packed acceptance gate from a clean tree at the recorded commit and re-record the receipt with `dirtyTaskFiles: false` before archiving.

findings.claim: The Next.js `DevelopmentGraphTools` snippet in the package README omits the unmount guard that the equivalent site-docs snippet includes, so the documented pattern can call `setHost` after the component unmounts.
findings.evidence: The package README `useEffect` does `void import(...).then((module) => setHost(() => module.EntityGraphDevtools));` with no cleanup, while `site/docs/guides/concepts/devtools.mdx` in the same diff wraps it with `let active = true; ... if (active) setHost(...); return () => { active = false; };` — the two published copies of the same recommended pattern disagree.
findings.suggested_fix: Copy the `active`-flag version from the site docs into the package README so both published snippets are identical.
